text:
PagerDuty Bot: [PAGER] Sev 2 alert - private-vpc-1234 GPU queue growth and autoscaler failures. Affected cluster: private-vpc-1234, customer: AcmeGames (acme-42). Paging #incidents and on-call.

Alex: Ack, I'm on-call. Starting triage.

PagerDuty Bot: Alert details: queue_length: 1200 -> 1500, avg_token_latency: 12s, autoscaler events: 'scale up rejected' x13. Pages: Alex, Maya.

Maya: Looking at metrics now. GPU pod Pending count is high, scheduler backlog increasing. Logs show repeated 'InsufficientInstanceCapacity' and a bunch of init container image pull failures.

Sam: Pulled relevant logs from cluster:
```
autoscaler: scale request for nodegroup acme-gpu-ng denied: quota limit reached
kubelet[pid]: Pulling image "private.repo.company/monitoring-agent:1.2" -> ImagePullBackOff
cloud-init: RunInstances failed: InsufficientInstanceCapacity
```

Jen: Confirmed on control plane: several new nodes stuck in Pending > 15m. The init container hitting rate limits on our private image registry for that customer's account. Also seeing a customer-side config: maxNodes: 12 in their cluster config (they're at 12).

Lee: So two limiting factors: cloud capacity/quota and a hard customer-side maxNodes cap. Autoscaler is following config and can't exceed 12; cloud API also failing new instance requests sporadically.

Alex: Customer impact? John from CS?

John (Customer Support): AcmeGames reports widespread 503s on /v1/recs/batch and elevated error rate on realtime endpoints. They've escalated to their ops team. Several customers reported job timeouts. This is visible on their dashboard.

Maya: Immediate mitigations proposal:
- increase cluster maxNodes from 12 -> 18 temporarily (requires emergency override),
- patch init image to use public mirror to avoid registry rate-limits,
- trigger manual scale while we watch cloud capacity,
- reroute low-priority batch traffic to hosted pool to reduce load on private cluster.

Alex: Can we change their maxNodes without legal approval? We have an emergency response SLA that permits temporary overrides with CS notice. John, confirm we can proceed and we'll notify the customer.

John (Customer Support): Customer OK with emergency increase if it reduces impact. They asked for ETA and will alert their SREs.

Sam: Commands I plan to run:
```
# patch autoscaler config map to bump max nodes
kubectl patch cm acme-autoscaler -n private --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_nodes":"18"}}'
# quick manual scale trigger (AWS example)
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name acme-gpu-asg --desired-capacity 16 --honor-cooldown
```

Jen: Before scaling, fix imagepulls so new nodes don't stall:
```
kubectl set image daemonset/cluster-init monitor=quay.io/redwood/monitor:latest -n private
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/cluster-init -n private
```
This will let init complete without hitting private registry limits.

Lee: Applying the image patch now. Patching... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Lee: Patch applied, rollout started. New nodes are starting to pull public image.

PagerDuty Bot: Notice: on-call handover to Maya scheduled at 02:30 UTC.

Sam: Manual scale issued to desired 16. Watching ASG events.

Sam: ASG events: 4 new instances launch -> Instance status: Initializing -> Registered to k8s.

Maya: New nodes Ready, kube-scheduler placing GPU pods. Queue length trending down: 1200 -> 480 in 8m. Latency improving but still elevated.

Alex: Routing low-priority batch traffic to hosted pool to reduce inbound load. Executing route change now.

Alex: curl -X POST https://internal-routing.redwood/api/routes -d '{"route":"/v1/recs/batch","target":"hosted:batch-pool","dry_run":false}'

Alex: Route change accepted. Traffic shift started.

Maya: Observed background queue drop and prioritised requests getting scheduled. Priority-1 latencies back to acceptable range; background jobs still draining.

Sam: Queue numbers: 1200 -> 180 in 12m after new nodes and routing change. Error rate on /v1/recs down 80%.

John (Customer Support): Customer updated. They confirmed partial recovery; still seeing occasional 503s under heavy load but much better. Appreciative of rapid response.

Alex: Root cause hypothesis so far: combination of (1) customer-side hard maxNodes cap preventing autoscaler from exceeding allocation, (2) image pull rate-limiting on private registry stalling node bootstrap, and (3) transient cloud capacity/quota errors (InsufficientInstanceCapacity). Need postmortem to confirm chain.

Maya: Immediate next steps:
- keep autoscaler maxNodes at 18 for 2 hours, then roll back to agreed level with customer signoff,
- add image mirror fallback in cluster-init (public fallback),
- add synthetic checks for node bootstrap success and image pull latency for private registries,
- add autoscaler fallback policy to route to hosted models when private cluster is saturated.

Alex: I'll create the incident ticket and assign postmortem to Maya. Quick doc link: https://redwood/incident/2390001234 (do not edit until handoff complete).

Maya: I accept postmortem ownership. Handoff notes: mitigation applied, customer notified, monitoring corralled. Will run RCA and timeline.

Alex: Handoff complete. I'm leaving incident channel. Thanks team.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident status -> Partial mitigation. Assigned to Maya for RCA and postmortem. If regressions occur re-escalate to Sev1.

Maya: Confirming ownership and will publish postmortem within 72 hours. Adding action items to backlog (pre-warm pools, registry mirror, autoscaler fallback). :memo: 

Sam: Logging the commands and output to incident artifacts in tracker.

Jen: I'll open a change MR for cluster-init to add mirror and a timeout guard.

Lee: I'll follow up on quotas with cloud infra team and request soft quota increase for that region for these private clusters.

John (Customer Support): I'll send a final follow-up note to the customer once we have postmortem ETA.

Maya: Leaving monitoring runbook notes and will ask oncall to page if queue > 300 after rollback.

Alex: :thumbsup: Great work, team.
